JavaScript · Fundamentals

What is the difference between Promise.all() and Promise.allSettled()?

Answer

  • Promise.all(promises): resolves with an array of all values when all fulfil; rejects immediately when any one rejects (fail-fast). Use when all results are required (e.g. page needs all data).
  • Promise.allSettled(promises): waits for all to settle and never rejects; returns [{status: 'fulfilled', value}, {status: 'rejected', reason}]. Use when calls are independent and you want partial results (e.g. dashboard widgets).
const results = await Promise.allSettled([getUser(), getOrders()]);
results.forEach(r => r.status === 'fulfilled' ? use(r.value) : log(r.reason));

Also: Promise.race (first to settle) and Promise.any (first to fulfil; rejects only if all reject).
